title: My day and the week

parent.learn: Parts of the day: morning, afternoon, evening, night.
parent.why: The sun rises in the morning and sets in the evening; this daily cycle is how we first understand time.
We wake up before we go to school. Putting events in order is the first step to planning and to telling stories.

parent.learn: The 7 days of the week, in order.
parent.why: The week repeats like a pattern: after Sunday, Monday comes again. Knowing the order lets the child work out tomorrow and yesterday.
Tomorrow is the day after today; yesterday is the day before. These are just “after” and “before” for days.

parent.learn: Some things take a long time, some a short time.
parent.why: Sleeping takes many hours; blinking takes less than a second. Comparing durations comes before reading a clock.

ask: What did you do this morning? What will you do tonight?
What do you do first: brush your teeth or eat breakfast?
Say the days of the week.
What day is today? What day will tomorrow be?
Which takes longer: having a bath or eating a biscuit?
Which day do you like best? Why?

rounds.t: When does the sun come up?
rounds.h: The sun rises in the morning and the day begins.

rounds.t: When do we go to sleep?
rounds.h: When it gets dark at night, we sleep.
We have to wake up before we can go to school.

rounds.t: The moon and stars come out at…
rounds.h: We see the moon and stars in the dark night sky.
Lunch is the middle meal, around the middle of the day.

rounds.t: How many days are in a week?
rounds.h: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days.
Saturday, then Sunday — the end of the week.

rounds.t: Which day is a holiday for most schools?
rounds.h: Most schools are closed on Sunday.

rounds.t: Today is Wednesday. Tomorrow will be…
rounds.h: Tomorrow is the next day: after Wednesday comes Thursday.
Today is the day after yesterday: after Sunday comes Monday.
We sleep for many hours; brushing takes only a few minutes.
A blink is over in a moment; lunch takes a while.
We look at a clock to know what time it is.
